title: Frontier G: automated discovery rediscovers rho; apparent sub-1/2 exponent is setup amortisation
question: Frontier G (ECDLP-54, automated algorithm discovery): evolutionary search over a 19-op DSL (group ops, x comparisons and bits, bounded hash table, counters) on 10-12-bit training curves, tested on held-out sizes 13-16 and fresh curves: nothing beats exponent 1/2 once fixed setup cost is modelled. Evolved champion s1 (rho-like: table-stepped walk keyed by low bits of x plus hash collision detection, success 1.00) literally passed the pre-registered rule (test-A beta 0.375 [0.326,0.426] < BSGS lower99 0.434), but hand DP-rho in the same DSL scores 0.334 [0.295,0.372]; on a fresh curve per size both fit cost ~ 1.77 sqrt(r) + 136 (PI refit), so the low naive exponent is setup amortisation. s3 beta 0.456 [0.391,0.519]; s0, s2 not solvers. No program rediscovered BSGS.
rationale: User directive 2026-11-03 (give everything): replace human-designed candidates by automated search.

Methodological lesson (PI): naive log-log exponent fits at r <= 2^16 are biased low by additive setup cost (hand rho 0.327, BSGS 0.438 though both are Theta(sqrt r)); any future speedup claim must fit alpha sqrt(r) + gamma (or compare against a same-implementation rho control) before reporting an exponent.
next_action: Closed for this DSL and size range. If resumed: larger sizes (2^17-2^20, faster curve generation), alpha sqrt(r)+gamma fitness, and richer primitives.
notes: PI re-ran supp.py random_s1 via exec: identical output through 16 bits (both runs stopped by the 270 s timeout, exit 124); PI fitted alpha sqrt(r)+gamma: rho_dp 1.77 sqrt(r)+136, s1 1.77 sqrt(r)+136, BSGS 1.51 sqrt(r)+33.
